Source slide page 2 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
  Introduction

A string is a collection of characters or a sequence of characters.

Creating strings is as straightforward as assigning a value to a variable.
Ex:
       var1 = ““   # empty string.
       var1 = "python"
       var1 = “”” this is python”””

Source slide page 3 (extracted text):

Characteristics

o A string has zero or more characters.
  >>> str1=" “            >>> str1="p"
  >>> str2="python“      >>> str3 = ‘’’python pro ‘’’
o Each character of a string can be accessed by using the index that starts from 0. Negative
   indicesindices areare allowedallowed.
Example:-
  >>> str2[0]
        'p’
  >>> str2[-1]
        ‘n’
o The index value can be an expression that is computed.
      >>> str2[2+3]
             'n’

 Characteristics

o Immutable – cannot modify the individual characters in a string. One cannot
  add, delete, or replace characters of a string.


Example:-

o Iterable: Traversing elements one by one.


Example:-

   forfor ii inin str2:str2:

   Output: p y t h o n

min and max functions as applied to strings return the smallest and largest character
respectivelyrespectively basedbased onon thethe underlyingunderlying UnicodeUnicode encodingencoding.

uppercase letters.
o  Example:-
   >>> str1="Python“

     'y'

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Common operators applied on string

Concatenation (+) operator can be used to add multiple strings together.
   >>> str1="Python“     >>> str2="Language"
   >>> str1+str2
   'PythonLanguage’


Repetition (*) operator returns True if a sequence with the specified value is present in
the string otherwise False.
  >>> str1="Python Programming"
  >>> str1*2
  'Python ProgrammingPython Programming'

Source slide page 10 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Common operators applied on string

Scope resolution (::) operator assigns the characters of string str1 into an
another string str2.
   >>> str1="Python Programming"
   >>> str2=str1[::]    // same as str2=str1
   >>> str2
   'PythonPython Programming’Programming
   >>> id(str1)
   1534440206336
   >>> id(str2)
   1534440206336

Source slide page 11 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 Common operators applied on string

Membership (in) operator returns True  if a sequence with the specified
value is present in the string otherwise False.
  >>> str2="Language"
  >>> "Lang" in "Language"
  True
  >>>>>> "Png"Png  inin "Language"Language
   False

Membership (not in) operator is used to repeat the string to a certain
length.
   >>> str1="Language"
   >>> "LAN" not in str1
   True
   >>> "Lang" not in str1
   False

Source slide page 12 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Common operators applied on string

The slice operator s[start:end] returns the substring starting with index start,
  up to but not including index end.

o Example:-
      >>> s = 'Monty Python’
      >>>>>> s[0:4]s[0:4]
        Mont
      >>> s[6:7]
         P
      >>> s[6:20]
          Python

Specific functions of string

startswith(prefix,start,end) returns True if string starts with the given prefix
otherwise returns False.
   prefix – A string that needs to be checked.
   start – starting position where prefix is needed to be checked within the
string.
   end-end EndingEnding positionposition wherewhere prefixprefix isis neededneeded toto bebe checkedchecked withinwithin thethe stringstring.
   Ex:-
  >>> str1.startswith("W",0)
   True
  >>> str1.startswith("W",1)
   False
  >>> str1.startswith("App",5,8)
  True
  >>> str1.startswith("App",6,9)
  False

Source slide page 16 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Specific functions of string

endswith(search_string,start,end) returns True if original string ends with the
search_string otherwise returns False.
   search_string – A string to be searched.
   start – starting position of the string from where the search_string is to be
searched.
   end-end EndingEnding positionposition ofof thethe stringstring toto bebe consideredconsidered forfor searchingsearching.
   Ex:-
  >>> str1="Welcome to Python Class“      >>> str1.endswith("Class",18,22)
  >>> str1.endswith("Class")                  False

   True                                    True
  >>> str1.endswith("Class",18)

  >>> str1.endswith("Class",19)

Source slide page 17 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Specific functions of string

o There are a number of methods specific to strings in addition to the
   general sequence operations.
o String processing involves search.
o The find(substring,start,end) method returns the index location of the
    first occurrence of a specified substring. If not found, returms -1.
   Substring-Substring TheThe substringsubstring toto searchsearch forfor.
   start – where to start the search. Default is 0.
  end – where to end the search. Default is 0.
>>> s3="chocolate“                          >>>s3.find(“c”,4,9)
>>> s3.find("c")                             -1
0
>>> s3.find("z")                              >>>s3.find(“c”,3,9)
-1                                  3

Source slide page 18 (extracted text):

Specific functions of string

o The rfind(substring,start,end) method returns the index location of the
   last occurrence of a specified substring. If not found, returns -1.
   Substring- The substring to search for.
   start – where to start the search. Default is 0.
  end – where to end the search. Default is 0.
  >>>>>> s3="chocolate“s3  chocolate
  >>> s3.rfind("c")
  3
  >>> s3.rfind("c",-6,-1)
  3

   -1                                         -1

Specific functions of string

o The strip(characters) method removes characters from both left and right
  based on the argument.
o The lstrip(characters) method removes characters from left based on the
   argument.
o The rstrip(characters) method removes characters from right based on the
  argumentargument.

  >>> str1="      Welcome to Python class       "

  'Welcome to Python class’

The replace method produces a new string with every occurrence of a given
substring within the original string replaced with another.
o >>> s1.replace("a","b")
   'whbtsbpp'
o >>> s1.replace("a","b",1)

o >>> s1.replace("a","b",2)

o >>> s1.replace("a","b",0)

Specific functions of string

The title() method returns a string where the first character in every word is
upper case.
o >>> str1="people education society"
  >>> str1.title()
   'People Education Society’

The capitalize() method returns a string where the first character is upper
case, and the rest is lower case.
  >>> s1="Python"
  >>> s1.capitalize()
   'Python'

Source slide page 23 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Specific functions of string

The join() method takes all items in an iterable and joins them into one string.
A string must be specified as the separator.

Example:-
   >>> s1="abc"
   >>> s2="xyz"
   >>> s1.join(s2)
   'xabcyabcz’

Source slide page 24 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Specific functions of string

The split() method splits a string into a list.

Example:-
o >>> str1="When someone is lost, dare to help them find the way."
  >>> str1.split()
   ['When', 'someone', 'is', 'lost,', 'dare', 'to', 'help', 'them', 'find', 'the', 'way.’]
o >>> str1.split("i")
  ['When someone ', 's lost, dare to help them f', 'nd the way.’]
o >>> str1.split("i",1)

o >>> str1.split("i",1,2)

Source slide page 25 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Specific functions of string

o The isspace() method  returns “True”  if  all characters in the string are
  whitespace characters, Otherwise, It returns “False”.
  >>> s1=“ “                             >>> s1="543a"
  >>> s1.isspace()                         >>> s1.isspace()

o The ljust() method will left align the string, using a specified character and
   returns a new string
  >>> s3="chocolate"
  >>> s3.ljust(20)
   'chocolate          ‘
  >>> s3.ljust(20,"#")

Source slide page 26 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Specific functions of string

o The rjust() method will right align the string, using a specified character
  and returns a new string
  >>> s3="chocolate"
  >>> s3.rjust(20)
     '      chocolate’
  >>>>>> s3s3.rjust(20,rjust(20 "$")$ )
   '$$$$$$$$$$$chocolate'
o The center() method will center align the string, using a specified character
  and returns a new string.
  >>> s3="chocolate"
  >>> s3.center(20)
     '   chocolate     ‘
  >>> s3.center(20,'*’)

Source slide page 27 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Specific functions of string

o The zfill() method adds zeros (0) at the beginning of the string, until it
   reaches the specified length.
  >>> s3.zfill(10)
   '0chocolate’
  >>> s3.zfill(20)

9), else    False.
